text.p: UK food and drinks giant Grand Metropolitan Plc said on Friday that trading conditions had remained "broadly unchanged" since it released half-year results in May.
Its Pillsbury baking unit in the United States was continuing to trade well, with gains in volumes, market share and operating profit.

GrandMet said profits at its drinks subsidiary,IDV, which were flat year-on-year in the first half, were ahead to date, reflecting comparable volume growth of three percent and an improved price environment, particularly in the United States.

For Pillsbury Brands, organic volume growth for the year so far was four percent, GrandMet said in its Autumn trading statement. However, volume growth in higher margin refrigerated baked goods, breakfast products and pizzas was seven percent.
Pillsbury Specialty Brands, established to develop Pet's major brands in the U.S. -- Old El Paso and Progresso -- was trading ahead of last year.
But while Old El Paso had achieved market share growth in Mexican meals, category growth in Mexican foods was running at about four percent -- less than expected.

The integration into Pillsbury was practically complete and cost savings, estimated to be in excess of 50 million stg at the time of the purchase, were still expected to come in in line with expectations.
GrandMet said its hamburger chain Burger King was still outperforming the U.S. fast food industry, with year to date comparable store sales growth above 2.5 percent.

Recent acquisitions of La Saltena in Argentina, Pasta House in Australia and Frescarini in Brazil were "encouraging", GrandMet said, adding that its Haagen-Dazs ice cream had achieved good growth in consumer takeaway.

Local currency profits in Japan were ahead of last year and Europe had continued to improve to almost break-even. In GrandMet Foods, European profits were running at similar levels to last year, it noted.

Profit growth has been restored in IDV's European business, with the UK benefiting from the continued growth of Baileys liqueur, price rises on major brands and the successful launch of Smirnoff Mule.
In Spain, J&B whisky volumes were ahead of last year and a further price rise was implemented in May, GrandMet said.

GrandMet said cash flow remained strong, although, as previously indicated, would be below last year's level in 1995/96, due to higher capital expenditure, the lower level of property disposals and higher tax payments.
Proceeds from the major business disposals would not be received until the 1996/97 financial year. Year end borrowings are expected to be below three billion stg.
GrandMet said it remained committed to achieving solid, organic profit through focus of "effort and investment" in its core branded food and drinks businesses.
"This will be achieved through appropriate advertising support for core brands, new product development, focused capital expenditure and expansion into emerging markets," it stated.
